full_original_abstract_TeX:
We prove that the complex Zariski closure of the exposed points of any
finite Minkowski sum of ellipsoidal discs of dimension at least two is
irreducible. No genericity or full-dimensionality assumption is needed.
This proves the exposed-point irreducibility conjecture stated by Meroni
in the 2023 Oberwolfach report. Under an explicit generic condition on
the summand spans, we also prove that this closure equals the purely
nonlinear part defined by Gesmundo and Meroni, thereby proving their
2022 irreducibility conjecture. The proof uses a connected real-analytic
support-point parametrization. A nongeneric example shows why the two
varieties must be distinguished.

exact_claim.objects: Finite N>=1 Minkowski sum of centered ellipsoidal balls D_i=A_i(B^mi) in real R^d, each actual rank m_i>=2. A_i is injective from its minimal real parameter space; no assumption of injective global support map.
exact_claim.main: The complex Zariski closure E(D) of all exposed points (unique maxima of some nonzero real linear functional) is irreducible, for every such configuration. No genericity/full-dimensionality of D is required.
exact_claim.generic_identification: For full-dimensional D with GP: dimension of sum_(i in J) L_i equals min(d,sum_(i in J) m_i) for every subset J, S(D)=E(D), where S is complex Zariski closure of (sum relative boundaries of D_i) intersect ambient boundary of D. GP is nonempty real Zariski open on full-rank matrices of fixed sizes, with Vandermonde witness.
boundaries: Rank-one summands cannot be included without qualification; interval and disk+segment give reducible E.
Main theorem allows coincident spans, repeated discs, dependent radicals, singular or noninjective support maps, and lower-dimensional sums.
S=E is not asserted for arbitrary nongeneric full-dimensional D; explicit three-disc counterexample separated by polynomial.
No general irreducibility claim for the full complex critical locus, nor degree or birationality claim.
For generic purely nonlinear conjecture, full dimensionality or the source convention of reducing ambient space to span is load-bearing.
No global complex square-root branch is chosen; positive real roots on the connected real domain are used.

independent_chain.mechanism: Vanishing ideal of real-analytic image of nonempty connected open U is prime over C: if PQ vanishes and P does not, Q vanishes on a nonempty open patch and hence all connected U by real-analytic identity theorem. Separate real and imaginary parts.
independent_chain.prior_credit: Standard identity-theorem principle; cited real-Zariski form must be checked, not claimed new.

independent_chain.mechanism: Each excluded kernel A_i^T has codimension m_i>=2. For x,y off all kernels choose z off M_i+R x and M_i+R y, all proper; the two straight segments avoid every excluded kernel. Finite union is closed and cannot fill R^d.

Minkowski support faces add; sum is singleton iff each summand face is. For regular u, unique point p_i=Q_i u/sqrt(u^TQ_i u); otherwise whole positive-dimensional D_i is a face. Thus Exp(D)=F(U) exactly, not merely a dense subset. Positive radicands give global real analyticity on U.

Any boundary-generator decomposition has common supporting u. Inactive summand spans lie in u-perp; GP forces direct sum with total dimension<=d-1. Concatenated transpose surjective, so choose w with A_j^T w=v_j for all inactive unit boundary parameters. For positive epsilon, inactive support points are exactly prescribed, active ones converge. Every generator of S is a real limit of exposed points; algebraic closure E is Euclidean closed.

Every failed maximal rank condition is determinantal, finite subsets. Distinct real Vandermonde columns realize all ranks simultaneously; ambient sum>=d ensures full span. Need literal original genericity/ambient convention comparison.

Rank-one failures verified conceptually. In nongeneric3D sum2B_xy+B_xz, e3 is generated by relative boundaries and belongs to a support face. All exposed points satisfy P=(X²+Y²+Z²-5)²-4(4-Y²)(1-Z²)=0, while P(e3)=16, proving algebraic separation.
